description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:312-335

  /// Implementations SHOULD return quickly (in-process struct
  /// construction, possibly off a cached per-account record) —
  /// this method is called on the hot Space/set path.
  fn limits(&self, _caller: &Self::CallerCtx, _account_id: &jmap_types::Id) -> ChatLimits {
      ChatLimits::default()
  }

The (caller, account_id) arguments are documented as intentionally
plumbed for future per-account variation (Free vs Pro tier,
multi-tenant SaaS). The doc names exactly the production case the
seam exists for. But the method is SYNC, so any production backend
that looks up caps from a database or service:

- Must block_on / tokio::task::block_in_place inside, which
  introduces runtime-pinning hazards in a Send context.
- Must pre-cache every (account_id, ...) combination in memory at
  startup, which doesn't scale to multi-tenant SaaS with many
  accounts.
- Must accept that the cache might be stale (which is fine for caps,
  arguably) — but the contract gives the consumer no way to opt
  into async refresh.

Three relevant points:

1. The trait's other hooks (slow_mode_check, is_contact_blocked,
   may_set_custom_emoji, expire_message, apply_space_patch,
   apply_space_metadata_patch) are all async. limits is the odd
   one out.

2. Once the trait method ships sync, flipping to async is a
   major-version-break. Backend implementors who built the sync
   shape are stuck.

3. The doc disclaims this with 'SHOULD return quickly', but
   'quickly' is ambiguous: sync-quickly-with-cache vs
   async-quickly-with-await are wire-incompatible.

Fix:
  fn limits(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = ChatLimits> + Send {
      async { ChatLimits::default() }
  }

The default impl stays trivial. Backends that want sync return an
already-resolved future; backends that need async get the option.
The hot-path SHOULD-return-quickly guidance survives unchanged in
the rustdoc; it just becomes 'return a ready future quickly' for
backends that have local cache.

(Note: jmap-mail-server's older max_<thing> methods predate this
convention and are individually sync; workspace AGENTS.md
explicitly says NOT to retroactively propagate this struct shape
into mail-server. The fix here is local to chat-server.)
title: API contract: ChatBackend::limits is sync, locks out async per-account lookups
